title: Passive but accessible:  Studied information is not actively stored in working memory, yet attended regardless of anticipated load
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from a working memory experiment investigating whether previously studied (learned) information is actively maintained in working memory or remains passively accessible. Participants performed a visual working memory task involving memorization and probing of colored objects under varying expectations of memory load (extra-load vs low-load), while EEG was recorded to assess neural indices of active storage and attentional allocation. The study addresses how anticipated memory load influences the encoding and retrieval of studied versus novel information.
methods_description: Each trial began with a fixation dot for a jittered ITI (600-1000 ms), followed by a first memory screen (1000 ms) showing lateral objects to be memorized (studied or novel), balanced by objects on the opposite side. After a 1400 ms interstimulus interval, a second memory screen (1000 ms) presented additional novel items above and below fixation, with probability of appearance manipulated between extra-load (80% present) and low-load (20% present) conditions. After a 400 ms interval, a probe appeared and participants reported the object's color via continuous mouse movement along a randomly rotated color wheel. Feedback on angular error was given for 400 ms, with corrective color feedback (1000 ms) for studied objects with errors greater than 40°.
